column1: # Shen T., Gao T., Lin W., Gu A. (2012). Determination of CO2 Solubility in Saturated Liquid CH4 + N2 and CH4 + C2H6 Mixtures
# above Atmospheric Pressure. J. Chem. Eng. Data 57(8), 2296-2303. DOI 10.1021/je3002859 (paywalled; not read).
# SLVE: liquid CO2 mole fraction and pressure at solid-liquid-vapour coexistence, static analytic, 112.0 to 169.9 K.
# Sets 1-2: CH4 + CO2, 9 points (x_CO2 0.000213 to 0.02896, 93 to 2315 kPa). Sets 3-4: CH4 + N2 solvent (x_CH4 of the solvent
# 0.9 to 0.98) + CO2, 27 points. Sets 5-6: CH4 + C2H6 solvent + CO2, 27 points. Each point appears twice (pressure row and
# composition row), both keyed by T and the solvent fraction.
# Holdout role: P5/G5 liquidus (CO2 solubility in liquid CH4) far below the CO2 triple point.
# Source: NIST TRC ThermoML Archive (IUPAC ThermoML), https://trc.nist.gov/ThermoML/10.1021/je3002859.xml, retrieved 2026-09-25;
# archive DOI 10.18434/mds2-2422. TRC terms: no warranty by the publisher, editors or NIST/TRC; TRC requests that works
# using ThermoML Archive data cite them. The XML is TRC's compilation of the paper's tables, not the paper itself.
# Flattened with thermoml_to_tsv.py (this folder): one row per property value, digits exactly as in the XML.
# U95 = nCombExpandUncertValue, expanded uncertainty at 95 % assessed by the TRC data-file compiler (not the authors' own
# statement unless the paper gives the same number). Labels abbreviated: fluid/liquid/gas/crystal, CO2/CH4/N2/C2H6.
